fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ~$4.50 x 19x = $85.5, weight 0.5), EV-based FCF yield (FY28 FCF ~$2.45B at 4.8% less ~$3.8B net debt = $82, weight 0.3) and EV/EBITDA (FY28 EBITDA ~$3.1B x 15.5x less ~$3.8B net debt = $77, weight 0.2); all on 575M non-GAAP diluted shares; blend ~$82.8, rounded to $83.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Bottom-up FY28 (Mar-2028): revenue ~$7.3B (consensus $7.43B, range $6.99-8.39B), non-GAAP GM 65% (LT model; Dec-qtr guided flat at 66-67%), op margin ~40% -> op income ~$2.92B, interest ~$180M, non-GAAP tax ~7.5-8% -> net ~$2.53B / 575M shares = ~$4.41 (vs consensus $4.58). NTM EPS as of Sep-2027 (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) ~$4.50 after a cycle haircut vs consensus roll-forward (~$4.7). x 19x (mid-cycle; peers NXPI ~15x, ON ~24x, TXN/ADI ~28-32x; 10-yr UST ~5.1% caps multiples) = $85.5

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$2.45B (company FCF before ~$111M/yr preferred dividend; Q1 FY27 FCF $498M on $1.485B sales, capex ~$100-150M/yr); required FCF yield on EV 4.8% -> EV ~$51B; less Sep-2027 net debt ~$3.8B ($5.09B at Jun-2026 less ~$250-300M/qtr paydown after ~$1.1B/yr common+preferred dividends) -> equity ~$47.2B / 575M = $82

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 non-GAAP EBITDA ~$3.1B (op income ~$2.92B + ~$0.2B depreciation; ~42.5% margin on $7.3B) x 15.5x = ~$48B EV; less ~$3.8B net debt -> ~$44.3B / 575M = $77

bear.story: Upcycle peaks around mid-2027 (roughly 8 quarters from its start), as the market begins pricing FY29: bookings slip below 1, outsourced-capacity lead times normalize and some customers destock, price increases stall, GM drifts toward ~61-62% and FY29 EPS expectations fall toward ~$3.3; semis derate further with 10-yr yields above 5%; stock ~15-16x trough-ish EPS. Less likely in the next 2-3 quarters given the 25-day distributor inventory, but a live risk at the horizon.

base.story: Recovery continues at a slowing rate: FY28 revenue ~$7.2-7.4B, GM 65-66%, NTM EPS ~$4.5-4.6 at the horizon, net debt falls to ~$3.8B (<2x EBITDA) and buybacks may restart; stock ~19x NTM plus ~2.3% dividend.

bull.story: Extended cycle with AI/data-center, PCIe Gen6/retimers, Hailo edge AI and industrial/defense strength; supply constraints ease and revenue reaches ~$2B/qtr, NTM EPS ~$5.5+, capital returns resume, semis re-rate; ~22-23x on $5.5.

thesis_break_reason: A close near $52 (-34%, ~11.5x FY28 consensus of $4.58) would mean the market is pricing an outright reversal of the recovery: book-to-bill below 1, guidance cut with GM heading back toward 60%, distributor inventory rebuilding from 25 days, or financing/leverage stress; below ~$62.5 the mandatory convertible also adds dilution (up to 29.1M shares below ~$51). I keep $52 rather than the supervisor's $55 because with 50% realized vol a -30% move to $55 is less than one annual standard deviation and the stock traded at $48.52 within the past year, so $55 could still be sector/rates noise.

catalysts.event: Q2 FY27 earnings (guide $1.589-1.618B sales, 66-67% GM, $0.91-0.95 EPS; consensus $0.93) and December-quarter guidance (consensus $1.62B, $0.94); test of flat 66-67% GM claim
Q3 FY27 earnings; seasonality and whether the Aug/Sep price increase sticks
Q4 FY27 earnings and FY28 outlook; possible buyback resumption once net leverage falls further
Q1 FY28 earnings; cycle-duration test around ~8 quarters into the upcycle
Rates (10-yr UST ~5.1%) and semiconductor sector sentiment / AI capex after the July-2026 selloff; TXN/NXPI/ADI/ON read-throughs
Hailo integration (closed 2026-09-21), J Capital short thesis on data-center revenue, COO departure

key_uncertainties: Timing of the cycle peak: near-term channel is lean (25 days distributor inventory, no double ordering per CFO), but an ~8-quarter upcycle would be maturing right at the horizon when the market prices FY29
Sustainability of 66-67% GM as one-time licensing and inventory-repricing gains roll off (CFO says price increase and lower underutilization offset them in the December quarter)
Sector multiple with 10-yr yields above 5% and post-AI-boom semis derating; 50% realized vol
Data-center growth credibility versus short-seller skepticism
Pace of deleveraging: only ~$250-300M/qtr after dividends; buybacks paused
Outsourced foundry/OSAT constraints capping revenue upside
reasoning: Round 2 update. The supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified, moved my inputs up modestly. (1) FY28 consensus EPS is $4.58 on $7.43B revenue (Alpha Vantage, 25 analysts, up from $4.19 60 days ago, 20 up / 1 down revisions in 30 days); my round-1 $6.8B revenue was below the lowest estimate ($6.985B), so I rebuilt FY28 at ~$7.3B. (2) Non-GAAP tax is ~7.5%, which with 65% GM and ~40% op margin gives ~$4.41 FY28 on 575M shares; I set NTM EPS at the horizon at ~$4.50 (up from $4.40), still below the consensus roll-forward as cycle discipline. (3) Net debt was $5.09B in June and falls ~$250-300M/qtr after dividends, so ~$3.8B by Sep-2027 (vs my $4.0B). (4) At Citi (2026-09-09) the CFO guided GM roughly flat at 66-67% into December, called distributor inventory low at 25 days and said there is no evidence of significant customer stocking; internal lead times are steady, and the stretch is at outsourced capacity. That lowers near-term channel-unwind risk, so I cut the bear weight from 25% to 20% and the low-median ladder component from 20% to 17% (its median moved from $70 to $66 and its sigma widened, so it now stands for a sharper but less likely mid-2027 reversal). I did not raise the multiple: the 10-yr UST at ~5.14% and the sector derating keep me at 19x, and I trimmed the EV/EBITDA multiple to 15.5x. Fair value $83 (from $82): P/E $85.5, FCF-yield $82, EV/EBITDA $77. This is below the supervisor's $85 because I haircut EPS a bit more (bottom-up ~$4.41 vs consensus $4.58) and use EV-based rather than equity FCF yield. Scenarios: bear $52 (20%), base $87 (55%), bull $125 (25%), probability-weighted ~$89 before a ~2.3% dividend. Ladder: a mixture of lognormals, 83% median $86 with sigma 0.39 and 17% median $66 with sigma 0.58. This keeps a fat left tail consistent with 50% realized vol and semis cyclicality. The ladder median is ~$83.3 (from ~$81), P(>=79) is 0.55 and P(>=106) is 0.28. Analyst mean PT ~$100 is evidence of sell-side optimism, not an anchor. Research was limited to 4 follow-up queries in round 2.
